subject.title: feat(linux): native gateway transport for Quick Chat — device identity, TLS pinning, ack-driven sends

question: Should `openclaw-linux` receive the existing native-app direct-local silent-pairing authorization class, with the same operator scopes and device-token lifecycle as macOS/iOS/Android?
rationale: The branch intentionally expands a Gateway admission and device-pairing trust boundary; code review can verify mechanics, but only maintainers can confirm that this client identity should permanently receive that authority.

options.title: Approve the native trust class
options.body: Confirm that Linux Quick Chat is a first-party native UI peer and retain the direct-local silent-pairing behavior after the mechanical fixes land.

options.title: Require explicit Linux approval
options.body: Keep the Linux client in the protocol but require dashboard approval for its initial pairing until a narrower trust model is designed.

recommendation.title: Approve the native trust class
recommendation.body: Confirm that Linux Quick Chat is a first-party native UI peer and retain the direct-local silent-pairing behavior after the mechanical fixes land.
